chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥarīz, said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the muḥṣan. He said: “It is one who commits zina while he has that which suffices him.”

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنِ: a legally protected person in the context of zina rulings
key_terms.مَا يُغْنِيهِ: that which suffices him lawfully and removes need
key_terms.يَزْنِي: commits zina, meaning illicit sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: Who is considered a muḥṣan in the rulings of zina according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the muḥṣan in the context of zina as one who commits fornication or adultery despite having access to what suffices him lawfully. It serves as a jurisprudential clarification relevant to the legal classification and rulings concerning zina.
